In the second generation of computers, vacuum tubes (also known as thermionic valves) were replaced by transistors.

Why this was a major upgrade:

  • Heat: They generated significantly less heat, making the systems more reliable.

  • Power: They required much less electricity to operate.

  • Speed: They allowed for faster switching, which increased the overall processing speed of the computer.

This shift occurred roughly between 1956 and 1963. Following this, the third generation replaced individual transistors with Integrated Circuits (ICs).

uni-unilag-com101-bank-0922.explanation:
To convert a long binary number to hexadecimal, the easiest way is to group the digits into sets of four, starting from the right. Each group of four binary digits corresponds to exactly one hexadecimal digit.

Step 1: Group by 4 (from right to left)

The binary number is $10010111101100100111_{2}$.

We break it into groups of four:

1001 | 0111 | 1011 | 0010 | 0111

Step 2: Convert each group to Hex

Using the standard conversion (8-4-2-1 rule):

  • 1001: $8 + 0 + 0 + 1 = 9$ $\rightarrow$ 9

  • 0111: $0 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 7$ $\rightarrow$ 7

  • 1011: $8 + 0 + 2 + 1 = 11$ $\rightarrow$ B (In hex, 10=A, 11=B, 12=C...)

  • 0010: $0 + 0 + 2 + 0 = 2$ $\rightarrow$ 2

  • 0111: $0 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 7$ $\rightarrow$ 7

Step 3: Combine the results

Putting them all together:

9 7 B 2 7

The hexadecimal equivalent of $10010111101100100111_{2}$ is $97B27_{16}$.
